# WHY THIS TABLE EXISTS, WHEN guard-hook-fixtures.tsv ALREADY PASSES
# Every row of guard-hook-fixtures.tsv runs with NO repository policy file, so
# it pins the framework's defaults and nothing else. Two consequences, both
# 1. The `humanOwned*` switches are documented, supported delegations. What the
#    guard does once a repository has turned one OFF was never tested at all —
#    and that is exactly where the framework makes its strongest promise:
#    "History rewriting and force pushes are denied regardless of this setting."
# 2. Asserting only the DECISION cannot tell which rule produced it. `git push
#    --force` is denied twice over under default policy: once as a force push,
#    once as an ordinary Git write. Deleting the force-push branch entirely left
#    all 135 rows green — and under `humanOwnedGitWrites: false` the same
#    command then returned `allow`. A test suite that stays green while a real
#    safety property is deleted is not protecting it.
# The reason-substring column is what closes that: it asserts WHICH rule fired,
# so the policy-independent branch cannot be shadowed by a policy-governed one.
# The profiles are defined once in the runner, not here, because a profile is a
# configuration file rather than a row.
# defaults — the framework floor, with no repository policy file at all.
